newsitem.title: Czech republic: TENNIS-SELES RETIRES FROM BRNO EXHIBITION.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SELES RETIRES FROM BRNO EXHIBITION.

text.p: World co-number two Monica Seles retired after the first set of her debut at the Komercni Banka Open women's on Wednesday, forced off the court once again by a nagging shoulder injury.
Seles, who had been given a bye into the semifinals of the exhibition event, showed no signs of trouble early in her match against Katerina Habsudova of Slovakia.
But as the set entered a tie break in the first set, she appeared to begin to favour her left shoulder, losing pace on her groundstrokes and especially her serve.
After losing the tie break 3-7, the 22-year-old American informed officials she could not continue.

"I am really very sorry that I cannot finish the match. I tried to play as hard as I could, but it's just not possible. I hope I can repay you by coming back next year," she told the crowd to a roar of applause.
After winning the Australian Open to start the season, Seles tore a muscle in her left, serving shoulder and has struggled to maintain her form since.
Seles lost in the quarter-finals at the French Open and in the second round at Wimbledon before clawing her way to the U.S. Open final where she lost to Steffi Graf.
Last month her season of disappoinment and pain ended early when she was forced to retire during the first set of the year-ending Chase Championship due to the same injury.

Before the Chase Championship Seles had ruled out surgery on her shoulder for the rest of the year, opting instead for a strict therapy regiment, and said she planned to defend her Australian Open title.
She did not say whether she had changed her mind on the topic of surgery following the Brno event.
